function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: list
function.description: List files and directories in a cross-platform way, similar to ls -al output. Prefer this over shell ls/dir.

path.description: Directory or file path to list (relative or absolute). Defaults to current workspace root.

all.description: Whether to include hidden and dot entries (default true).

long.description: Whether to include ls -al style long format lines (default true).

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: exec
function.description: Execute shell commands with background continuation for work that starts now. Use yieldMs/background to continue later via process tool. For long-running work started now, rely on automatic completion wake when it is enabled and the command emits output or fails; otherwise use process to confirm completion. Use process whenever you need logs, status, input, or intervention. Do not use exec sleep or delay loops for reminders or deferred follow-ups; use cron instead. Use pty=true for TTY-required commands (terminal UIs, coding agents).

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, kills process on expiry)

pty.description: Run in a pseudo-terminal (PTY) when available (TTY-required CLIs, coding agents)

elevated.description: Run on the host with elevated permissions (if allowed)

function.name: wechat_reply_media
function.description: Reply to the current WeChat conversation with a file. Reads the file from disk and sends it as an image, document, or video. Supported types — image: PNG/JPG/GIF/WEBP; file: any document including DOC/DOCX/PDF/XLS/XLSX/PPT/PPTX/TXT/CSV/ZIP and more; video: MP4. Use this after generating or writing a file that should be delivered to the user.

media_type.description: Kind of content to send: 'image' (PNG/JPG/GIF/WEBP), 'file' (any document: DOC/DOCX/PDF/XLS/XLSX/PPT/PPTX/TXT/CSV/ZIP/etc.), or 'video' (MP4).

path.description: Local file path to the file to send.

file_name.description: Display filename shown to the recipient. Defaults to the basename of path. Recommended when media_type is 'file' to ensure the correct extension is shown.

caption.description: Optional caption text attached to the content (supported for video).

function.name: wechat_send_media
function.description: Proactively send a file to a specific WeChat user by user_id. Supports images, documents (DOC/DOCX/PDF/XLS/XLSX/PPT/PPTX/TXT/CSV/ZIP/etc.), and videos. Requires a prior context_token from an existing conversation with that user.

user_id.description: WeChat user ID of the recipient.

media_type.description: Kind of content to send: 'image' (PNG/JPG/GIF/WEBP), 'file' (any document: DOC/DOCX/PDF/XLS/XLSX/PPT/PPTX/TXT/CSV/ZIP/etc.), or 'video' (MP4).

path.description: Local file path to the file to send.

file_name.description: Display filename shown to the recipient. Defaults to the basename of path. Recommended when media_type is 'file' to ensure the correct extension is shown.

caption.description: Optional caption text attached to the content (supported for video).

function.name: generate_image
function.description: Generate an image from a text prompt using OpenRouter's image generation API. Saves the image to a local file and returns the file path. After generating, use wechat_reply_media with media_type='image' and the returned path to send it to the user.

prompt.description: Text description of the image to generate.

output_path.description: Optional local path to save the image. Defaults to outputs/<timestamp>.png.
